identity.name: WAAREEENER
identity.industry: Solar PV Manufacturing (integrated module → cell → ingot/wafer → polysilicon) + Energy Transition Platform

summary.oneLiner: India's #1 solar module maker is morphing from a module exporter into a fully backward-integrated multi-energy platform (poly→wafer→cell→module + inverters, transformers, BESS, electrolysers), riding record US realizations and a Rs.60,000 cr order book while the China cell-price reset structurally favors Indian supply.

one-line thesis: India's #1 solar module maker is morphing from a module exporter into a fully backward-integrated multi-energy platform (poly→wafer→cell→module + inverters, transformers, BESS, electrolysers), riding record US realizations and a Rs.60,000 cr order book while the China cell-price reset structurally favors Indian supply.
financial scorecard: One-offs: Rs. ~294 cr exceptional provision (US investigation, lawyer-advised, no demand raised yet). IRA 45X credit booked ~Rs. 80 cr in Q3 (recorded at 90% of ¢7/Wp, only on partial volume) vs ~Rs.162 cr prior quarter.
guidance: FY26 EBITDA: clear visibility of surpassing the prior Rs. 5,500–6,000 cr guidance. (Verify next quarter: 9M EBITDA already ~Rs.4,332 cr, so Q4 run-rate alone implies the upper band is being beaten.)
FY27: declined to give a number; "premature." Stresses structural margin stability.
Cell utilization to reach 85–90% within 3–4 months (currently ~80% daily run-rate vs ~56% quarter-average optics).
order book & pipeline: Order book ~Rs. 60,000 cr (as of call date, includes the recently-disclosed 2.1 GW); pipeline >100 GW.
Geographic split of order book ~65% overseas / 35% domestic.
Implied Q3 order inflow ~Rs. 20,500 cr; ~80% solar, rest mostly retail/EPC. Transformers order book Rs. 245 cr; inverters similar small size.
Domestic mix ~80–85% non-DCR currently (shifting toward DCR as captive cells ramp). Cells consumed almost entirely captively.
Orders deemed firm only with advance (5–15%, contract-to-contract); retail shipped only against full payment.
segment / subsidiary: US (Texas): Q3 ~275 MW produced, ~313 MW sold; US top-line >Rs. 2,000 cr. Meyer Burger HJT assets acquired & ramping. No US cell mfg yet (actively considering). Realizations north of ¢28–30/Wp on some orders (tariff partly passed through).
Oman (United Solar Holdings): non-Chinese fully-traceable polysilicon; production expected to start this quarter (Q4 FY26); uptake agreements + financial closure done.
growth verticals / optionality: Inverters: 3 GW Sarodhi (Gujarat) phase-1 commissioned; +1 GW phase-2 by FY27. India inverter market ~4x by 2035.
Transformers: expanding to 20,000 MVA, Capex ~Rs.192 cr; order book Rs.245 cr incl. a global MNC order.
BESS: 20 GWh facility ready by FY28; indigenizing anode/cathode/electrolyte; ~$1 bn capex → ~$1.5–2 bn potential revenue (1.5–2x asset turn); first 10 MW pilot order taken.
Green hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser, Capex ~Rs.676 cr, live by FY27, PLI Rs.444 cr.

Renewable power infra: PPAs 713 MW signed; 6.1 GW connectivity secured; ~3,500 acres acquired + ~13,500 acres under acquisition (≈5–6 GW land). Full-stack platform sold to infra funds/PE who lack land-aggregation mandate.
Raised ~Rs. 1,000 cr equity for the 20 GWh battery facility.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin managed via back-to-back cell tying; commodity risk avoided where possible (pass-through is contract-dependent — "sometimes on us").
Silver impact <9% on a module basis; silver ~25% of cell cost.
India cell cost of production ~¢7/Wp now (scale benefits to come).
Realizations: non-DCR module ~Rs.18.5/Wp (India non-DCR ~Rs.14–15; US ~Rs.24–25+); DCR module ~Rs.23–24/Wp.

Margin levers: rising DCR content, daily utilization gains, operating leverage, price hikes if needed. Mgmt commits to holding/improving margins despite peers (RenewSys/Jackson) flagging need for ~25% price hikes.
capex / expansion: All of modules, cells, ingots & wafers to be operationalized by FY27.
New 10 GW cell facility: ~4 months per line ramp (first lines ~6 months) given 5.4 GW learning curve.

10 GW ingot & wafer (FY27): crystal-puller sourcing diversified beyond China; restrictions eased; in negotiations (won't disclose vendors). ASM Technologies & Rana Semiconductor noted by analyst as Indian equipment makers.
capital allocation: ~Rs. 1,000 cr equity raised for BESS. Heavy reinvestment across the full value chain ("Waaree 2.0"). Prudent working-capital posture (advances/full-payment-before-ship). No dividend discussion on call.
risks & watch-items: US anti-dumping / circumvention investigation (Indonesia/Laos routing) — Rs.294 cr provision booked pre-emptively; outcome unresolved.
Commodity risk: silver & cell-price inflation (China cells ¢4–4.5 → ~¢6/Wp).
Cell utilization optics (quarter-avg 56% vs daily 80%) — execution to be proven next quarter.
Tariff regime "continuously evolving"; reliant on cell country-of-origin rules.
India PPA logjam (~42 GW stuck) — transmission/transformer/bay/land bottlenecks; demand timing risk.
New-vertical (BESS/H2/inverter) economics still "embryonic" — no audited numbers.
management quality / tone: Highly promotional, superlative-heavy ("stellar," "record-breaking," "two big dogs"). CEO candid on declining FY27 guidance and on US-investigation provisioning. CFO precise and numbers-fluent. A mid-call audio glitch occurred; mgmt compensated with extra time. Confident, slightly salesy.
non-obvious takeaways: The China export-rebate taper (pushing cell prices up ~50%) is framed as a positive — it "proves up" Chinese costs and makes Indian supply globally competitive.
US is the margin engine: ¢28–30/Wp realizations dwarf India's ~Rs.18.5/Wp non-DCR; IRA 45X booked conservatively (90% of ¢7, partial volume) — implies hidden upside / cushion.
Mgmt is deliberately moving away from quoting GW (mix-driven), signaling EPC/turnkey/non-module revenue is becoming material and harder to benchmark.
Captive cell consumption + rising DCR is the structural margin story, not spot pricing.
"Overcapacity is a myth" stance: 9M module/cell demand (35 GW) already exceeds full prior-year; bets demand keeps "galloping."
qoq change log: Order book rising toward Rs.60,000 cr (incl. newly disclosed 2.1 GW); pipeline >100 GW.
Cell production +35% QoQ; daily cell utilization ~80% (from quarter-avg ~56%), targeting 85–90% in 3–4 months via G12R upgrade.
IRA 45X credit booked ~Rs.80 cr this quarter vs ~Rs.162 cr prior quarter (conservative recognition).
US realizations escalated to ¢28–30/Wp on some orders (vs prior ¢24–25) on tariff pass-through + mix.

New: Rs.294 cr exceptional provision for US investigation; ~Rs.1,000 cr equity raised for 20 GWh BESS; Oman polysilicon (United Solar Holdings) production to start in Q4 FY26; transformer order book Rs.245 cr incl. global MNC; first 10 MW BESS pilot order; Meyer Burger US HJT assets ramping.

themes.title: Solar PV cell-to-module manufacturing
themes.need: Solar module/cell manufacturers ride capacity ramp, ALMM/DCR protection and an order-book build-out - a manufacturing thesis distinct from firm-power/FDRE tender economics or merchant storage arbitrage. Q1FY27 quantified the DCR arbitrage: EMMVEE grew revenue 51% to INR 1,555cr with EBITDA margin up to 35.2% and PAT +103% on a 9.9 GW order book, with DCR modules earning INR 8.5-9/W of EBITDA against INR 2-2.5/W for non-DCR - a 3-4x per-watt gap that structurally separates integrated cell makers from module assemblers. The offset is order timing: SWSOLAR booked a record INR 13,000cr unexecuted order value on a landmark USD 560m Egypt win (1,000 MW solar + 600 MWh BESS) yet revenue still fell 10% YoY, and flagged that industry orders concluded only ~INR 6,400cr against the >INR 20,000cr expected, deferred by DCR/module-price uncertainty.
themes.driver: DCR cell/module capacity commissioning and the ALMM List-2 per-watt spread; domestic ordering restarting after two slow quarters (SWSOLAR); order-book conversion.
